description: ``write_guard.check_powershell`` had only two ``Remove-Item`` patterns — no protected-zone write extraction for PowerShell. Every write cmdlet (``Set-Content``, ``Out-File``, ``Add-Content``, ``Tee-Object``, ``New-Item -Path X -ItemType File``) and PowerShell's own ``>`` / ``>>`` redirect form passed the hook against protected destinations. PowerShell cmdlet names and flag names are case-insensitive, so a lowercase or mixed-case form (``set-content -path …``) was equally available. Fix: ``_PS_PATH_FLAG_RE`` captures the value after ``-Path`` / ``-FilePath`` / ``-LiteralPath``; ``_PS_POSITIONAL_RE`` captures the first positional argument of ``Set-Content`` / ``Out-File`` / ``Add-Content``; ``_REDIRECT_RE`` (shared with bash) handles ``>`` and ``>>``. A new ``check_powershell_for_protected_mutations`` runs them through ``_is_protected`` in a dedicated PowerShell branch of ``main()``.
